Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

RBBayes 1.0.0

Release preparation

  • Corrected package website links and made previously disabled examples runnable.
  • Expanded the package description and identified the copyright holder.

Tutorial-driven interface revision

  • Model constructors take the Gamma prior directly: bt_model(shape_lambda = 2, rate_lambda = 1), bt_sbm_model(shape_lambda, rate_lambda, item_clustering), and likewise for PL models. The strengths are i.i.d. a priori; latent_strength() objects are still accepted (deprecated). The default BT prior is now Gamma(4, exp(digamma(4))), matching BT–SBM.
  • gnedin_prior(gnedin_hyper = 0.5); gnedin_hyperparameter is a deprecated alias.
  • Notation: z_i is the block of item i; lambda_i (BT) and lambda_k (BT–SBM) are strengths.
  • New names: posterior_K_table() (was pretty_table_K_distribution(), which remains) and plot_ordered_adjacency() (wraps plot_block_adjacency()).
  • MCMC parameters are named after items: rel_strength[<item>] (share of total strength), lambda[<item>], n_item_blocks, n_ranking_groups. Old names q[i], theta[i], K_item, K_ranking are still accepted in pars.
  • summary() returns a summary.btsbm_fit with descriptive field names and a readable print method (data size, priors, MCMC run, posterior K and partition for block models, relative strengths otherwise).
  • Plackett–Luce strengths are reported as shares summing to one by default (pl_identifiability("sum")), replacing the geometric-mean scale. strength_summary() and plot_strength_summary() use relative strengths.
  • New: partition_point_estimate(), credible_ball() / plot_credible_ball() (Wade & Ghahramani credible balls; optional mcclust.ext cross-check), block_stability(), prob_stronger() / plot_prob_stronger() for Pr(lambda_i > lambda_j | y).
  • plot_assignment_probabilities() uses a diverging colour scale centred at 0.5, prints probabilities, and states the conditioning K and number of draws.
  • plot_posterior_similarity() orders items by the estimated partition and outlines its blocks.
  • Block colours: colour-blind-safe palette for up to 8 blocks, distinct HCL colours beyond; short user palettes are interpolated instead of failing.
  • salso, mcclust and kableExtra moved to Suggests; a built-in VI search is used when salso is absent, so installation is lighter for students.
  • tennis_tiered_toy() defaults to strengths c(12, 6, 2, 1) and the edge list carries the true tiers in attr(, "truth").
  • A hands-on tutorial is installed at system.file("tutorial", "RBBayes-tutorial.Rmd", package = "RBBayes").

Package rename

  • The installable package is now RBBayes. Use library(RBBayes) after installing from lapo-santi/RBBayes; the repository address is unchanged.
  • Existing function names and fitted-object classes remain compatible.

Pairwise-data workflow updates

  • as_bt_data() also accepts directed edge-list data frames, with explicit winner, loser and optional count columns. Repeated edges are aggregated.
  • tennis_tiered_toy() accepts generating block counts, strength vectors, player counts and names, and can return an aggregated edge list.
  • dirichlet_process_K_var() provides a dedicated prior-variance function; prior_variance_K() delegates to it for Dirichlet-process priors.

Development interface updates

  • Use fit_model() as the common BT/PL fitting entry point. Earlier fitter names remain available for compatibility.
  • Convert fits directly with as.matrix(), as.array(), coda::as.mcmc() and coda::as.mcmc.list(). Relative item strengths and occupied-group counts provide fixed-dimensional draws for coda and bayesplot.
  • Combine independent runs using as_draws_array() and as_mcmc_chains(), preserving chain identity and checking compatible data and model definitions.

BTSBM 0.1.0

Initial CRAN submission

  • Initial release of BTSBM.
  • Added Gibbs samplers for Bradley-Terry stochastic block models.
  • Added posterior relabelling and partition summaries.
  • Added plotting utilities for adjacency, assignment uncertainty, lambda uncertainty, and rank intervals.
  • Added ATP demo data and introductory vignettes.
